1 OPINION
2
3 COYLE, Chair --The issue in this case is whether a purchaser of
4 farm and agricultural land is required to show, to the satisfaction
5 of the Assessor, that the land continues to qualify for open space
6 classification before the deed is recorded.
7
8 The facts are not in dispute. The matter is before us. on stipu-
9 lated facts and uncontradicted affidavits. The Ayres purchased an
10 80 -acre farm on San Juan Island. The farm had been taxed as open
11 space farm and agricultural land. The Ayres wished to continue the
12 agricultural use, and wished the property to remain in the open space
13 classification. The day before the sale transaction closed, the Ayres
14 signed a notice of continuance in open space classification. On the
15 closing day, the Ayres' representative presented the signed notice of
16 continuance to the Assessor. Because this was the first time the
17 Assessor had heard of the impending sale, he told the representative
18 that he would need more time and additional information, such as a
19 farm management plan, in order to determine if the property continued
20 to qualify for open space classification. The Ayres wished to have
21 the transaction close on that day. Therefore, they paid -the addi-
22 tional tax and penalties, and the deed was recorded.
23
24 The Ayres filed an appeal with the San Juan County Board of
25 Equalization ( Board of Equalization), seeking to have the land
26
27

1 continued in the open space classification. The Board of Equalization
2 ruled in favor of the Ayres. The Assessor appeals.
3
4 ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSIONS
5
6 Once land has been classified as open space farm and agricultural
7 land, it remains so until it ceases to be used for farm purposes ( RCW
84. 34. 080) or until certain events take place. One of those events is
9 the sale of the property to a new owner. RCW 84. 34. 108( 1)( c) requires
10 the Assessor to remove the land from open space classification upon:
11 Sale or transfer of all or a portion of such land to
a new owner, unless the new owner has signed a notice of
12 classification continuance, except transfer to an owner who
is an heir or devisee of a deceased owner shall not, by
13 itself, result in removal of classification. The notice of
continuance shall be on a form prepared by the department
14 of revenue. If the notice of continuance is not signed by
the new owner and attached to the real estate excise tax
15 affidavit, all additional taxes calculated pursuant to sub-
section ( 4) of this section shall become due and payable
16 by the seller or transferor at time of sale. The county
auditor shall not accept an instrument of conveyance of
17 classified land for filing or recording unless the new owner
has signed the notice of continuance or the additional tax
18 has been paid, as evidenced by the real estate excise- tax
stamp affixed thereto by the treasurer. The seller, trans-
19 feror, or new owner may appeal the new assessed valuation
calculated under subsection ( 4) of this section to the
20 county board of equalization. Jurisdiction is hereby con-
ferred on the county board of equalization to hear these
21 appeals . . . .
22
23 The Department of Revenue ( Department) has adopted rules to
24 implement this statute. The relevant rule, WAC 458- 30- 275, states:
25 1) Introduction. When land classified under chapter
84. 34 RCW is sold or transferred certain procedures must
26 be followed if the new owner wishes to keep the land in
27

1 its present classified status. This section explains the
required procedures and forms.
2 2) Definitions. For purposes of this section, the
following definitions apply:
3 a) " Affidavit" means the real estate excise tax affi-
davit that the department prescribes and furnishes to county
4 treasurers for use by the owner in reporting sales and/ or
transfers of classified land. The form will require the
5 signature, under the penalty of perjury, of the owner and
purchaser or transferee or agents of each. See chapter 82. 45
6 RCW and chapter 458- 61 WAC for more specific details.
b) " Notice of continuance" means the notice signed
7 when land classified as open space, farm and agricultural, or
timber land under the provisions of chapter 84. 34 RCW is sold
8 or transferred and when the new owner of the classified land
wishes to have the land remain classified under the provi-
9 sions of chapter 84. 34 RCW. This notice may be either part
of the real estate excise tax affidavit or a separate docu-
10 ment created by the department.
c) " Owner" means any person or persons having a fee
11 interest in a parcel of land, except when the land is subject
to a real estate contract and the vendee when the land is
12 subject to a real estate contract. For purposes of this
section, the owner or owners of classified land must all sign
13 the notice of classification continuance and/ or real estate
excise tax affidavit.
14 3) General requirements. When a parcel( s) of land
classified as open space, farm and agricultural, or timber
15 land under chapter 84. 34 RCW is sold or transferred and the
new owner wishes to keep the land in its classified status,
16 the new owner must:
a) Sign a notice of classification continuance that
17 is part of a real estate tax affidavit. ( See subsection ( 8)
of this section for a discussion regarding this affidavit);
18 and
b) Provide the assessor with a signed statement that
19 explains how the owner will use the parcel( s) of land so as
to continue its eligibility for classification under the
20 provisions of chapter 84. 34 RCW; and
c) Sign a separate notice of continuance prepared by
21 the department if the county has decided that it will require
new owners to submit such a form.
22 4) Assessor' s duties and authority related to sale or
transfers. When land classified under chapter 84. 34 RCW is
23 in the process of being sold or transferred, the new _owner
must sign a notice of continuance and the statement described
24 in subsection ( 3) of this section if he or she wishes the
land to remain classified. This notice of continuance and
25 signed statement shall be presented to the assessor who must
determine if the land will continue to be used in a manner
26 approved for classified status or if the land will not be
27

1 used in a manner consistent with the current use program.
The assessor shall be allowed a reasonable amount of time
2 to determine whether the classified use of the land will be
continued by the new owner.
3 a) Upon receipt of the notice of classification
continuance, the assessor may require the new owner to submit
4 additional information including, but not limited to, the
types of data listed in WAC 458- 30- 270.
5 b) Within fifteen calendar days of receiving the
notice of classification continuance, the signed statement,
6 and all requested information, the assessor shall determine
whether the land qualifies for continued classification as of
7 the date of conveyance.
c) The assessor may consult with the granting author-
8 ity to determine if the land will qualify for continued clas-
sification. The assessor and/ or the granting authority may
9 ask the owner to submit additional information and pertinent
data to ensure that the land will continue to be used for a
10 classified use.
d) No instrument of conveyance may be filed with the
11 county auditor or recorded unless:
i) The assessor has determined that the land will be
12 used for current use purposes and can continue to be classi-
fied within the current use program;
13 ii) If the land is no longer eligible to be classi-
fied within the current use program, the seller or trans-
14 feror has paid the additional tax, applicable interest, and
penalty;
15 iii) The land will be removed from classification
and the removal results solely from one of the exceptions
16 listed in RCW 84. 34. 108( 5) to the imposition of additional
tax, applicable interest, and penalty. See also WAC 458- 30-
17 300 that implements this statute; or
iv) In the case of a sale, a completed real estate
18 excise tax affidavit has been submitted to the treasurer of
the county in which the classified land is located. To be
19 complete the real estate excise tax affidavit must indicate
whether the land is classified under the provisions of
20 chapter 84. 34 RCW.
e) If land must be removed from classification
21 because it was sold or transferred as a result of any of
the occurrences or actions listed in RCW 84. 34. 108( 5), the
22 assessor shall:
i) Follow the standard procedures set forth in WAC
23 458- 30- 295 and 458- 30- 300 for removing the land from classi-
fication;
24 ii) Notify the county treasurer and the seller or
transferor that no additional tax, applicable interest, or
25 penalty are due as a result of the sale or transfer because
RCW 84. 34. 108( 5) specifically exempts the transaction from
26
27

the imposition of additional tax, applicable interest, and
penalty; and
iii) In the case of land acquired for conservation
purposes by any of the entities listed in RCW 84. 34. 108( 5)
f), inform the new owner or transferee that if the land
ceases to be used for the purposes enumerated in RCW 84. 34-
210 or 64. 04. 130, the additional tax, applicable interest,
and penalty will be due.
5) Timber land. When a parcel( s) of classified
timber land is sold or transferred, the new owner must submit
a timber management plan to the assessor in order to continue
the classification, in addition to the general requirements
listed in subsection ( 3) of this section. The assessor shall
send a copy of the timber management plan to the county
legislative authority of the county in which the classified
land is located. WAC 458- 30- 232 contains a list of the types
of additional information an assessor may require the new
owner to submit so that the assessor can determine if the
land will continue to be used to grow and harvest forest
crops for commercial purposes.
6) Farm and agricultural land. When a parcel( s) of
classified. farm and agricultural land is sold or transferred,
the new owner must comply with the general requirements set
forth in subsection ( 3) of this section. The size of the
parcel( s) of farm and agricultural land sold or transferred
will determine whether any additional requirements must also
be satisfied. A parcel( s) of land that is less than twenty
acres must produce a specified amount of income to remain
classified as farm and agricultural land. After all required
information is submitted, the assessor shall determine
whether the land qualifies for continued classification..
a) Twenty acres or more. If the parcel( s) sold or
transferred is twenty acres or more, the new owner must
satisfy the general requirements listed in subsection ( 3) of
this section.
b) Less than twenty acres. In a sale or transfer
involving less than twenty acres, the new owner will be
required to comply with the general requirements of sub-
section ( 3) of this section and may be asked to provide gross
income data relating to the productivity of the farm or
agricultural operation for three of the past five years.
This information regarding the earning or productive capacity
of the classified land will be used to determine if the land
meets the income criteria listed in chapter 84. 34 RCW and
this WAC chapter.
i) Minimum income limits are set forth in RCW 84-
34. 020( 2) ( b) ( i) and ( ii) for parcels that are at least five
but less than twenty acres in size and in RCW 84. 34. 020( 2)
c)( i) and ( ii) for parcels that are less than five acres in
size. Any sale or transfer of classified land, except to a
surviving spouse, subject to these income limits. See WAC

458- 30- 210( 3) and 458- 30- 317 for further information and
details.
ii) If, after January 1, 1993, classified land is sold
by an owner who applied for and was granted classification
prior to January 1, 1993, to a new owner, the minimum income
requirements specified in RCW 84. 34. 020( 2)( b)( ii) and ( c)( ii)
will be deferred for a period of three years. The new owner
must meet these minimum income limits at least once during
the three calendar years immediately following the sale or
transfer of the classified farm and agricultural land. For
example, if classification was granted in 1978 to a fifteen
acre parcel that produced a gross income of one hundred
thirty dollars per acre per year and the land is sold on
April 15, 1993, the minimum income requirements will be
deferred until 1996. By the end of 1996, the new owner must
provide proof that the parcel produced two hundred dollars
per acre at least one year during the three-year period
between 1993 and 1996. If the land has produced a. gross
income of two hundred dollars per acre the land will remain
classified as farm and agricultural land. If the land has
not produced this amount at least once during this three-year
period, the land shall be removed from classification and the
owner will be required to pay an additional tax, interest,
and penalty.
iii) If, after January 1, 1993, classified land is
sold by an owner who applied for and was granted classifi-
cation after January 1, 1993, the assessor will review the
information regarding the productivity of the land for three
out of the past five years to determine whether the minimum
income limits set forth in RCW 84. 34. 020( 2)( b)( ii) or ( c)( ii)
have been met. For example, if a ten acre parcel was granted
classification on May 1, 1993, and it is sold on February 23,
1994, the assessor will ask the seller and/ or buyer of the
classified land to provide information about the earning or
production capacity of the land for at least the five calen-
dar years preceding the sale ( i.e., 1989 through 1993). To
retain the current use classification, the land must have
produced a minimum of two hundred dollars per acre per year
at least three out of the five calendar years preceding the
date of sale.
c) Segregation of land. In a sale or transfer
involving a land segregation, the owner of the newly created
parcel( s), and the owner of the parcel( s) of land from which
the segregated land was taken must comply with the require-
ments of ( a) or ( b) of this subsection before the assessor
determines if the land qualifies for continued classifica-
tion.
7) New owner' s warranty. The new owner, upon signing
the notice of continuance, warrants that future use of the
land will conform to the provisions of chapter 84. 34 RCW and
this WAC chapter.

8) Real estate excise tax. Under the provisions of
chapter 82. 45 RCW whenever real property is sold or trans-
ferred an excise tax is imposed; the amount of this tax is
related to the selling price of the real property. Real
estate excise tax is due at the time of sale. This tax is
paid to and collected by the treasurer of the county where
the real property is located.
a) The seller or the buyer, or the agent of either,
of the real property must pay the excise tax and must submit
a signed real estate excise tax affidavit to the treasurer of
the county where the real property is located.
b) When the ownership of classified land is sold or
transferred to a new owner who intends to continue classifi-
cation of the land under the provisions of chapter 84. 34 RCW,
the new owner must make a notation of this intent on the
affidavit.
c) No instrument of sale or conveyance evidencing a
sale subject to the real estate excise tax may be accepted
by the county auditor for filing or recording until a stamp
is affixed to the affidavit by the treasurer that shows the
tax has been paid. The county treasurer shall not stamp the
instrument of sale or conveyance unless the assessor has
determined that the classified use of the land will be
continued or that the additional tax, interest, and/ or
penalty required under RCW 84. 34. 080 and 84. 34. 108, except
as exempted under RCW 84. 34. 070 or 84. 34. 108( 5), have been
collected.
Emphasis supplied.)
The statute, RCW 84. 34. 108( 1)( c) requires that the new owner file
a " notice of continuance" before the deed can be recorded with the
County Auditor. The main purpose of the statutory requirement for
filing a notice of continuance is to prevent the sort of unwelcome
surprise that results from being unaware that one' s newly purchased
land has previously been taxed under the Open Space Tax Act. If an
unwitting purchaser changes the use of the land, either intentionally,
such as by developing it for residential use, or unintentionally, such
as by ceasing to actively farm it, there will be a big property tax

bill forthcoming, which the purchaser did not consider when negoti-
ating a purchase price with the seller.
The statute says nothing about the Assessor having to review
the notice of continuance, approve the continued use of the property
for farm and agricultural purposes prior to recording the deed, or
otherwise participate in the sale of the property in any manner. The
Assessor argues that WAC 458- 30- 275( 4), however, interposes him in the
transaction. The rule states:
d) No instrument of conveyance may be filed with the
county auditor or recorded unless:
i) The assessor has determined that the land will be
used for current use purposes and can continue to be classi-
fied within the current use program;
or ( iv) In the case of a sale, a completed real estate
excise tax affidavit has been submitted to the treasurer of
the county in which the classified land is located. To be
complete the real estate excise tax affidavit must indicate
whether the land is classified under the provisions of
chapter 84. 34 RCW.
The question before us is whether the rule requires the Assessor
to sign off on the continued taxation of the property under the Open
Space Tax Act before the County Auditor can record the deed.
Before turning to this question, we first consider our authority
to consider the Ayres' argument that the rule is inconsistent with
legislative intent or in excess of the Department' s authority to
promulgate. The Assessor argues that this Board has no authority
to declare a rule adopted by the Department invalid for any reason.
See Seattle v. Department of Ecology, 37 Wn. App. 819, 683 P. 2d 244

1984); Snohomish County v. State, 69 Wn. App. 655, 850 P. 2d 546
1993) .
3
4 We need not decide this issue because this case is before us on
5 appeal from a decision of the Board of Equalization. The question is
6 whether the Board of Equalization has the authority to ignore or
7 declare invalid a rule promulgated by the Department. There is no
8 statute which expressly, or by necessary implication, gives the Board
9 of Equalization the authority to overturn or ignore the Department' s
10 rules. In fact, RCW 84. 08. 120 provides: " It shall be the duty of
11 every public officer to comply with any lawful order, rule or regu-
12 lation of the department of revenue made under the provisions of this
13 title."
14
15 We therefore conclude the Board of Equalization has no authority
16 to ignore the Department' s rules. It follows that in this particular
17 appeal, we have no authority to declare the Department' s rule, WAC
18 458- 30- 275, invalid.'
19
20 The remaining question concerns the construction to be given to
21 the language of the rule. The standard rules of statutory construc-
22 tion are employed to interpret administrative rules. State -v. Burke,
23 92 Wn. 2d 474, 598 P. 2d 395 ( 1979). Where the language is plain,
24
25
26 1 Given this result, we have no need to reach the issue of whether the
Department is a necessary party to this appeal.
27

unambiguous, and clear on its face, there is no room for construc-
tion, i. e., it must be construed according to its terms. Snow' s
Mobile Homes, Inc. v. Morgan, 80 Wn. 2d 283, 494 P. 2d 216 ( 1972); Auto
Drivers & Demonstrators Union Local No. 882 v. Department of Retire-
ment Systems, 92 Wn. 2d 415, 598 P. 2d 379 ( 1979). Here, the language
of WAC 458- 30- 275( 4)( d) is clear onits face with regard to cllaassssii--
ffiieedd land which is to remain taxed according to its current use: " No
instrument of conveyance may be filed with the county auditor or
recorded unless . . . [ t] he assessor has determined that the land will
be used for current use purposes and can continue to be classified
within the current use program . . " There are no exceptions. We,
thus, have no occasion to consider whether the purpose of the Depart-
ment in erecting an additional hurdle to the conveyancing of current
use property bears any relationship to the purpose of the Legislature
in enacting RCW 84. 34. 108( 1)( c).
The Ayres argue that the language of the rule is ambiguous. They
point out that WAC 458- 30- 275( 4)( d), above, which specifies that the
County Auditor cannot accept a deed for recording unless certain steps
have been taken, is couched in the alternative, i. e., the use of the
word " or" implies that in the case of a sale of current use property,
the only condition which must be satisfied is the signing of a notice
of continuance. Viewed in isolation and giving the Ayres the benefit
of the doubt, they might be correct that the use of the word " Cr"
creates an ambiguity. However, administrative rules, like statutes,

must be construed as a whole, not piecemeal. Donovick v. Seattle -
First National Bank, 111 Wn. 2d 413, 757 P. 2d 1378 ( 1988). Another
section dealing with the real estate excise tax, WAC 458- 30- 275( 8)( c)
states:
No instrument of sale or conveyance evidencing a sale
subject to the real estate excise tax may be accepted by the
county auditor for filing or recording until a stamp is
affixed to the affidavit by the treasurer that shows the tax
has been paid. The county treasurer shall not stamp the
instrument of sale or conveyance unless the assessor has
determined that the classified use of the land will be
continued or that the additional tax, interest, and/ or
penalty required under RCW 84. 34. 080' and 84. 34. 108, except
as exempted under RCW 84. 34. 070 or 84. 34. 108( 5), have been
collected.
The language in this subsection clearly and unequivocally
requires the Assessor to first make a determination that the land
will continue to be classified under the Open Space Tax Act before any
deed is recorded. To the extent that there may be ambiguity in other
sections of the rule, subsection ( 8)( c), above, dispels any doubt
about the Department' s directive to the County Auditor concerning the
recording of a deed conveying current use property.
We therefore conclude the Board of Equalization erred when it
ordered the Assessor to classify the land as farm and agricultural
land. The plain language of the rule supports the Assessor' s actions.
He simply followed the rule as it was written. -

FINDINGS OF FACT
2
3 1. In April 1999, Mary -Susan and Frederick R. Ayre purchased
4 two parcels of land totaling approximately 80 acres on San Juan
5 Island: tax parcels 340214001 and 340123002 ( the " Property"). The
6 Property was classified as open space under the farm and agricultural
7 current use tax provisions. The Ayres wished to continue the present
8 use of the Property and to maintain the open space tax classification.
9
10 2. The closing date for the sale was April 30, 1999. On
11 April 29, 1999, the Ayres signed the closing papers including the Real
12 Estate Excise Tax Affidavit where they checked and signed the notice
13 of continuance indicating their intent to continue the present classi-
14 fication. The Ayres did not contact the Assessor' s office prior to
15 the closing date to obtain a determination that the land qualified for
16 continuation in the open space current use tax program.
17
18 3. On April 30, 1999, at approximately 10 a. m., the Assessor' s
19 Office was presented with an Excise Tax Affidavit with a signed notice
20 of continuance indicating that the land was classified as open space
21 and that the Ayres wished to continue in the open space tax program.
22 This was the first notice of the sale received by the Assessor' s
23 Office.
24
25 4. The Assessor told the person representing the escrow company
26 that he would need additional information to determine if the property
27

qualified for continuation in the program before the conveyance could
be recorded. Without that information, the Assessor said, he would
have to remove the land from the open space tax classification and
require payment of back taxes and penalties before a deed could be
recorded. He was given the name and number of Tinya Bakotich of
Security Escrow in Bellevue.
5. The Assessor then spoke with Ms. Bakotich and told her
that, in order to record the deed, he would either need a . farm plan
explaining how the land was going to be used to produce agricultural
products for commercial purposes, or he would need payment of " roll
back taxes". He was given the number of Mrs. Ayre.
6. The Assessor spoke with Mrs. Ayre who confirmed that she and
her husband wished to keep the Property in the farm and agriculture
open space classification and planned to continue the present use of
the Property, including the growing of hay, some grazing of cattle,
and the maintenance of a trout pond. The Assessor told Mrs. Ayre
that, in order to continue the classification, he would need to make a
determination based on a written farm plan before the deed could be
recorded. He said that without a written farm plan and determination
of continued eligibility, the only other alternative for the deed to
be recorded was to remove the land from the farm and agricultural open
space classification and pay the back taxes.

7. The Assessor told Mrs. Ayre that she could fax a plan to him
in order for him to make a determination as to whether the land quali-
fied. The Ayres, however, concluded that they could not provide all
the information required in a farm plan and still close the sale that
day.
8. Around mid- day, the Assessor received a call from Ms.
Bakotich that the Ayres were going to remove the property from the
open space program. The Assessor told Ms. Bakotich that he would need
to have that request in writing signed by one of the Ayres.
9. Shortly afterwards, the Assessor received a signed authori-
zation from Mrs. Ayre to remove the land from open space tax classi-
fication. The Assessor removed the property from the farm and agri-
cultural open space classification and calculated the back taxes for
both parcels. The taxes, totaling $97, 669. 59, were paid by the escrow
company on the Ayres' behalf and the conveyance was recorded that
afternoon.
10. The Ayres would not have asked that the property be removed
from current use classification but for the Assessor' s refusal to
approve the continued classification at the time he was presented with
the notice of continuance.
11. After the sale closed, the Ayres appealed to the Board of
Equalization the Assessor' s decision to require a determination on the

continuation of open space tax classification before the conveyance
was recorded, or whether a signed notice of continuance was sufficient
for him to approve the conveyance for recording.
12. The Board of Equalization ruled in favor of the Ayres. The
Assessor filed his Notice of Appeal within thirty days of the Board of
Equalization' s decision.
Any Conclusion of Law which should be deemed a Finding of Fact is
hereby adopted as such.
From these findings, this Board comes to these
CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
1. The Board has jurisdiction over the parties and subject
matter of this appeal.
2. The issue in this appeal is ,whether a purchaser of land
classified as farm and agricultural for purposes of property taxation
according to the Open Space Tax Act, chapter 84. 34 RCW, is required to
obtain a determination from the Assessor that the land will be
eligible for continued classification as farm and agricultural land
prior to recording the deed with the County Auditor.

1 3. The statute, RCW 84. 34. 108, which deals with the sale of
2 land taxed according to its current use, requires only that the new
3 owner sign and file a notice of intent to continue the use of the
4 property in the appropriate current use classification before the
5 County Auditor can accept the deed for recording. The main purpose
6 underlying the enactment of this statutory provision is to provide
7 assurances that the buyer is aware ( 1) that the property is enrolled
8 in the current use program and ( 2) a change in use will trigger back
9 taxes and penalties.
10
11 4. The Department' s regulation, WAC 458- 30- 275, governs the
12 actions of the Assessor and the County Auditor in administering the
13 Open Space Tax Act with respect to the sale of property taxed accord-
14 ing to that act.
15
16 5. The language of the regulation is clear and unambiguous on
17 its face. It requires the Assessor to determine that the land will
18 be used for current use purposes and can continue to be classified
19 within the current use program prior to the time that any instrument
20 conveying such land can be accepted by the County Auditor for filing
21 or recording.
22
23 6. The Assessor acted in accordance with WAC 458- 30- 275 when
24 he required the purchasers to demonstrate to his satisfaction that
25 the land will be used for current use purposes and could continue to
26 be classified within the current use program before he noted such a
27

finding on the documents to be presented to the County Auditor. It
was not unreasonable for the Assessor to ask for additional informa-
tion concerning the use of the property.
7. The issue in this case is whether the Board of Equalization,
and not the Board of Tax Appeals, has the authority to ignore or
invalidate WAC 458- 30- 275.
8. The Board of Equalization has no authority to ignore or
invalidate WAC 458- 30- 275.
9. The Board of Equalization erred when it reversed the Asses-
sor' s determination.
Any Finding of Fact which should be deemed a Conclusion of Law is
hereby adopted as such.
From these conclusions, this Board enters this
DECISION
In accordance with RCW 84. 08. 130, this Board sets aside the
determination of the San Juan County Board of Equalization. The
matter is remanded to the San Juan County Assessor for reinstatement
of the original assessment.
